title: docs(herdr): pin a herdr version, and say what the controller does not do yet
body:
## What this changes

`docs/reference/herdr-provider.md` told readers the provider is "verified against
herdr 0.7.1+". The plus sign is the problem: 0.7.1 is the oldest release with a
recorded end-to-end validation, not a floor above which the surface is known to
hold. Nothing on the page said the surface had moved, and it has moved twice.

The page now makes the pinning argument from what actually happened:

- 0.7.4 and 0.7.5 altered commands the original adapter depended on.
- 0.8.0 renamed the code herdr returns for a pane with no named agent. That is
  the code the adapter reads to decide whether to paste a nudge instead of
  submitting it through the agent. Under the new spelling it stopped recognising
  that case, so the original failure went back to the caller and the paste never
  happened. Delivery reported an error rather than going quiet, but nothing in the
  build or the default suite went red, because the tests that drive a real binary
  are opt-in. The regression had to be noticed in the field.

So: pin a version in any shared environment, read herdr's own release list rather
than a version named in our docs, and after an upgrade run `make test-herdr-live`
and put a session through a full work cycle.

The page no longer names a current herdr release. A reference page cannot keep
that true, and an out-of-date "current version" reads as authoritative.

## The one known coverage gap

0.8.0 made herdr's agent registry detection-based, so the live journey that drives
the session-event stream waives itself when the installed herdr reports 0.8 or
later rather than asserting against a registry it no longer matches
([#5808](https://github.com/gastownhall/gascity/issues/5808)). That waiver reads
the version, not the registry: a herdr whose version cannot be read or parsed runs
the journey, and on 0.8 its registry assertions then fail. The other real-herdr
journeys (provider lifecycle, pane binding, activity, and the runtime conformance
suite) do run on 0.8; the kind-launch journey needs an installed `claude` binary as
well and skips without one. 0.7.1 remains the version the recorded end-to-end
validation ran against.

That distinction matters to a reader deciding whether to pilot this. "Not covered
on 0.8" would tell them to stay on 0.7; one waived journey out of seven tells them
what to watch instead.

## What is not wired yet

A new section, with one entry: the controller does not consume herdr's
session-event stream. herdr pushes session events and the provider implements
`runtime.SessionEventProvider`, but the only consumer today is the provider's own
activity reporting. The reconciler discovers session state on its periodic pass,
so a session that goes away is noticed on the next pass rather than when the event
arrives.

That costs latency rather than correctness, because each pass reads live state
rather than trusting an event. The delay is bounded by the reconcile interval only
while the controller keeps up; ticks run one at a time, so a busy controller
stretches it.

## Claims that came out of earlier drafts

Four statements were removed or corrected because they did not survive checking
against the code. Recording them here so they do not come back:

- That no error appeared when the 0.8.0 fallback broke. `deliverNudge` returns the
  original error; what was missing was anything making it fail a build.
- That the warm-reuse claim nudge bypasses session-store routing. It does not. The
  reconciler unwraps its typed session store (`session_reconciler.go`,
  `store := sessStore.Store`) and threads that down to the nudge, so both the read
  and the marker write already reach a relocated sessions backend.
- That the controller's added latency is the patrol interval. Ticks are serial, so
  the interval bounds it only while the controller keeps up.
- That the live journeys are waived on 0.8 and later. One of seven is, and that
  waiver is keyed to the version string rather than to the registry it is about.

Startup-prompt redelivery across a continuation-epoch bump was also dropped from
this page: it is a test-coverage gap rather than a behavior gap, and belongs with
the tests. Store-maintenance notifications repeating per interval is real and has
nothing to do with herdr.

## Test plan

Docs-only, one file, no Go changes.

```
go build ./... && go vet ./...
go test ./test/docsync/ ./internal/testpolicy/...
make check-docs
```

All green at this head. Every version-behavior claim on the page is cited to the
adapter code or to the test that covers it; the live-journey counts were derived
by listing the callers of the live gate and of the detection-based-registry skip.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

https://claude.ai/code/session_01CPcPXz8AxpyCCoDcK7Bu5W

<!-- mpr:issue-refs v1 -->

title: docs: gc-start-walkthrough and understanding-packs still put `path` under `[[rigs]]` in city.toml, which a schema-2 city now rejects
body:
## Symptom

Following `docs/troubleshooting/gc-start-walkthrough.mdx:243` (which says city.toml "is now the sole source of truth for rig locations") or `docs/guides/understanding-packs.md:134-136`, a reader writes

```toml
[[rigs]]
name = "demo"
path = "rigs/demo"
```

into city.toml. On a schema-2 city every `gc` command then fails:

```
pre-1.0 site-binding fields are no longer supported:
  - …/city.toml:6: unsupported pre-1.0 rig.path for rig "demo"; move it to .gc/site.toml (run `gc doctor --fix` if this is the root city.toml; otherwise add the binding manually and remove rig.path from the fragment)
see https://docs.gascityhall.com/guides/shareable-packs for migration details
```

## Root cause

The two passages predate the site-binding split. `internal/config/site_binding.go:142` (`LegacySiteBindingSurfaceError`, enabled by `compose.go:218-229` whenever the sibling `pack.toml` has `schema >= 2`) rejects `rig.path` outright; the location now lives in `.gc/site.toml`. The path-less `[[rigs]]` form used elsewhere in the docs is still accepted.

## Reproduction

Verified today on `main` (c374d5247): a scratch city with `[pack] name = "x"` / `schema = 2` in pack.toml and the block above in city.toml — `gc config show --city <dir>` prints the error verbatim. The same city without `path` loads (with the usual missing-import warnings).

## Fix candidates

1. Rewrite the two passages to the `.gc/site.toml` binding form and drop the "sole source of truth" sentence in the walkthrough. Docs only.
2. Same, plus delete `FormatConfig` in `test/acceptance/helpers/city.go:451`, which still emits the old shape and has no callers (dead code, so it breaks nothing today).

## Adjacent / out of scope

#1096 (PackV2 docs and implementation disagree) is the general version of this; this is one concrete instance with a verified error string. The quickstart itself is clean — it contains no TOML.

title: docs: propose Beads bootstrap compatibility gate
body:
## Summary

- Add a proposed bootstrap-compatibility companion design to the accepted Beads–Dolt contract redesign.
- Document the affected developer cohorts across packaged installs, source builds, upgrades, direct Beads use, automation, and local or external Dolt topologies.
- Propose one narrow invariant: before managed `bd init`, attest the selected initializer and prove its main-schema migration ceiling does not exceed the Beads reader linked into `gc`.
- Distinguish this gate from the existing cross-version contract-test proposal, `BD_BIN` pinning, release alignment, and Beads' shared-store migration consent work.

## Why

Issue #5348 reproduces a managed bootstrap where external `bd` creates schema v65 while Gas City's linked reader supports only v59. The existing Beads–Dolt design already establishes store identity, configuration authority, and lifecycle ownership; this proposal preserves that work and specifies the missing pre-bootstrap compatibility proof and no-publication regression.

This is a proposed design only. It does not change runtime behavior, add a configuration source, or impose one Beads version on independent projects.

Refs #5348.

## Testing

- [x] `make check-docs`
- [ ] `make check` (not run; documentation-only change)
- [ ] `make test-integration` (not applicable; no runtime behavior changed)

## Checklist

- [x] Linked an issue.
- [x] Added the proposal to the design index.
- [x] Identified alternatives, open maintainer decisions, and explicit non-goals.
- [x] Verified linked issue and PR states before publication.

title: docs(deps): record why the bd pin cannot move to a newer-numbered release
body:
## Summary

`deps.env` has long carried an instruction to promote `BD_VERSION` off `v1.1.0` "the day" beads publishes a release with the `--if-assignee`/`--if-status` conditional-write flags. beads has since shipped `v1.2.1` and `v1.2.2`, both dated after those flags landed in [beads#5008](https://github.com/gastownhall/beads/pull/5008), so the pin looked promotable. It isn't. The reason is one the old comment couldn't have anticipated: a beads tag's number doesn't order its capabilities.

beads cuts stable hotfixes off the `v1.1.0` line, which branched three weeks before the flags landed. That line is linear, it never merged to main, and both `v1.1.2` and the newest **stable** release `v1.2.2` sit on it. Neither one carries `--if-assignee` at all. `v1.2.1` is the first release that clears beads#5008 and it does carry both flags, but GitHub marks it a prerelease, so it doesn't meet the published bar this pin holds the installable default to.

So the pin stays where it is, and this change records why. It rewrites the `BD_VERSION` rationale in `deps.env`, names the two conditions that gate the next attempt, and sweeps the now-falsified "no published release has the flags" claim out of the five other places that asserted it: the `BD_PREV_VERSION` floor note, three comments across `internal/beads`, and the integration test's skip-and-fatal message. That last one is the one to look at, since it's the only site a human reads at runtime. **Comments and messages only: every pinned value is byte-identical to main.**

```mermaid
gitGraph
   commit id: "v1.1.0 base"
   branch hotfix-line
   commit id: "v1.1.2 (no flags)"
   commit id: "v1.2.2 (no flags, STABLE)"
   checkout main
   commit id: "beads#5008 flags"
   commit id: "v1.2.1 (flags, PRERELEASE)"
   commit id: "main"
```

## Risk

There's none to CI behaviour. No pinned version, SHA, or workflow `BD_VERSION` block moves, so every job installs exactly the bd it installed before. If CI goes red here, it won't be from this diff.

<details> <summary>Verification, and the two conditions that gate promotion</summary>

### How each claim was checked

Capability was measured against the published tarballs rather than inferred from version numbers, which is the same method the original comment used for `v1.1.2`:

| Release | Published | GitHub state | `bd update --help` names `--if-assignee` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `v1.1.2` | 2026-07-26 | stable | no |
| `v1.2.1` | 2026-08-11 | prerelease | **yes**, with the exit-13 semantics |
| `v1.2.2` | 2026-08-15 | stable | no |

Ancestry, via the compare API against `gastownhall/beads`:

- The hotfix line is linear and rooted before the flags: [`8e4e59d39`](https://github.com/gastownhall/beads/commit/8e4e59d39f3459a43cf21a3236a13eca4dd874f7) (2026-07-04) → +4 → `v1.1.2` → +7 → `v1.2.2`.
- Neither `v1.1.2` nor `v1.2.2` is an ancestor of beads `main`; each holds commits main does not.
- `v1.2.1` **is** an ancestor of beads `main` (main is 9 commits ahead, `v1.2.1` behind by none), and [`6e8af8bf8`](https://github.com/gastownhall/beads/commit/6e8af8bf8) is an ancestor of `v1.2.1`.

### Two conditions gate the next attempt

1. beads publishes a non-prerelease release cut from main, and its per-platform tarball SHAs go into `.github/scripts/install-bd-archive.sh`.
2. The fresh managed-Dolt bootstrap fix in [#5294](https://github.com/gastownhall/gascity/pull/5294) lands first. bd 1.2 added a legacy-workspace guard that refuses a pre-existing `.beads/dolt` carrying no version witness, so a fresh city under a 1.2 pin fails init until the witness is written for a proven-fresh database. That PR is open as of this writing.

Until both hold, the only flag-capable bd CI can obtain stays the source-built `BD_CURRENT_REF` cell, which is where the `ReleaseIfCurrent` CAS contract already runs.

### Every site the claim appeared in

| File | Site | Action |
|---|---|---|
| `deps.env` | `BD_VERSION` rationale | rewritten |
| `deps.env` | `BD_PREV_VERSION` floor note | corrected |
| `internal/beads/bdstore_conditional_release.go` | package comment | corrected |
| `internal/beads/bdstore.go` | `ReleaseIfCurrent` doc comment | corrected |
| `internal/beads/bdstore_conditional_release_integration_test.go` | test doc comment | corrected |
| `internal/beads/bdstore_conditional_release_integration_test.go` | skip and fatal message | corrected, runtime-visible |

Three further sites were checked and deliberately left alone, each re-verified as still true: the `.github/workflows/ci.yml` comment saying `BD_VERSION` "is a published release that predates it"; `bdstore_test.go`; and the graduation test, which is about `--if-revision`, a different flag absent from both `v1.2.1` and `v1.2.2`.

### Checks run

- `sh -n deps.env`, and sourcing it to confirm `BD_VERSION` and `BD_PREV_VERSION` read back unchanged.
- `diff` of the non-comment lines against `origin/main`: identical.
- `gofmt -l`, `go build ./internal/beads/...`, `go vet ./internal/beads/...`: all clean, before and after the round-1 sweep.
- Test packages under `internal/beads` compile; nothing asserts on any string touched.
- `git diff --check`: clean.

</details>

---

> • City: `city` · Agent: `local-core.builder-4`
> • On behalf of: @austinborn

title: AGENTS.md is written from one downstream fork's perspective
body:
The "Current integration mission" section in `AGENTS.md` is written from the perspective of one specific downstream fork — its mission, its local directory paths, and its remote naming — and none of that carries over to anyone else's fork or to this repo.

That raises a question that changes what actually needs fixing: is the intent that nobody works directly in `gastownhall/gascity`, and that all real work happens in forks that get integrated here? I'm assuming so, and if that's right I'm honestly fine with `AGENTS.md` being written from a downstream fork's point of view. But three things still don't hold up even under that assumption.

**It assumes I named the remote `upstream`.** The feature archaeology block runs `git fetch upstream`, `git diff upstream/main...HEAD`, `git range-diff upstream/main...HEAD`. That only works if I added `gastownhall/gascity` as a remote and happened to call it `upstream`. A fresh fork clone just has `origin`, and nothing in the doc says to add it. Either say so up front, or don't depend on the name.

**It has paths from someone's machine.** `/data/projects/gascity` and `/data/projects/t3code` aren't going to exist for anyone else.

**It states what the fork is for.** "This fork is integrating Gas City + T3 Code + a DoltLite-backed beads store." If everyone's working in a fork, every fork exists for its own reason — mine has nothing to do with T3 Code. Same with "Do not bury T3 Code or DoltLite assumptions in generic SDK paths," and "This fork has repeatedly lost working code during branch churn," which is one fork's history, not mine.

The rest of the section is good and I'd keep it: the archaeology workflow, "treat archived plans and audits as evidence, not gospel," and keeping backend-specific behavior behind the runtime/config/beads boundaries. That all applies to any fork. It just shouldn't be tied to one fork's mission.

For context, the section came in whole with a963419a1 (#2474), so I suspect it was never re-scoped rather than being deliberate.

If the fork-only assumption is right, this looks like a small edit — drop the specific mission and the local paths, and name the remote the git commands expect. Happy to send a PR. If it's not right, the section probably needs a bigger rethink, since read from inside this repo it's just false.

I searched for existing issues on this (`AGENTS.md`, "this fork", "integration mission", "T3 Code") and didn't find anything.

title: docs(session): clarify primed_at as delivery-attempted, not consumed (#5236)
body:
Fixes #5236.

## What's misleading

`primed_at` is stamped when delivery was *selected and runtime start succeeded* — but several doc comments described this as "confirmed delivered" / "actually delivers," which reads as proof the agent consumed the prompt. It isn't proof of that: the issue's own qualifying incident had a worker holding `primed_at` while its trigger bead stayed open/unassigned until a manual nudge forced the claim.

## Fix — comment/doc-string only, zero behavior or schema change

- `internal/session/lifecycle_transition.go` — `PrimedAtMetadataKey`'s doc said "confirmed delivered" with no caveat; added that "confirmed" means transport succeeded, not consumption, and pointed at trigger-bead assignment as the real work-started signal.
- `cmd/gc/prompt_delivery.go` — `promptDeliveryResult`/`Delivered` docs said "actually delivered it," but `promptDelivery()` does no I/O at all (pure routing decision, per its own existing doc) — clarified `Delivered` means "a mechanism was selected."
- `cmd/gc/session_lifecycle_parallel.go` — `promptDelivered` field doc said "actually delivers the rendered startup prompt" (one of the issue's own evidence citations) — same fix.

**Deliberately left `session_level_converge.go` untouched**, even though it also uses "CONFIRMED" language for `primedAt`: that's the S19 Stage-1 migration module ("nothing reads the action list yet ... until Stage 3 wires the act loop"), and its terminology is already precisely scoped within its own durable-world/runtime-world framework — it separately tracks `primedEnv` as "delivered this runtime but may not yet be durably recorded," meaning it already distinguishes the two states this issue wants clarified. Touching an in-progress migration module's carefully-established vocabulary without Stage 3/4 context felt like the wrong call. `internal/runtime/herdr/provider.go` (the issue's other evidence citation) was already correctly worded — no change needed there either.

## Verification

`go test ./internal/session/... -run 'Primed|Priming|Prompt'` and `go test ./cmd/gc/... -run 'PromptDelivery|Primed|Priming'` both green (comment-only, no regressions); gofmt clean; `go vet` clean on changed + dependent packages; `go build ./...` clean.

title: docs(dispatch): work-formula selection guide + v2 --on semantics; fix digest-generate mislisting
body:
## Summary

Documentation-only update to the `core` pack's `gc-dispatch` skill, closing two
gaps surfaced by the gas-city formula-adoption audit (gci-7x4):

1. **Variant-selection guidance** — a new *"Choosing a work formula"* decision
   guide (isolation × handoff table) covering `mol-do-work` vs `mol-scoped-work`
   vs `mol-polecat-work`, plus the `mol-polecat-commit` / `mol-polecat-report`
   siblings. Also documents `mol-scoped-work`, which the skill did not list at
   all.
2. **v2 `--on` / `-f` semantics** — the dispatch sections described the v1
   model ("creates a molecule wisp on the bead"). Updated to the v2 contract:
   a formula declaring `formula_compiler = ">=2.0.0"` starts a **workflow**
   (workflow-root + auto-convoy + work bead) whose step DAG and handoff
   metadata persist as beads; v1 formulas still instantiate a wisp. Adds the
   rule that convoy-referencing formulas (those using `{{convoy_id}}` or a
   drain step) must launch onto a convoy — which `--on` provides.
3. **digest-generate mislisting** — `mol-digest-generate` was listed among the
   patrols "auto-poured by agent startup prompts." It is not: it is driven by
   the `digest-generate` order on a 24h cooldown. Removed from the patrol list
   and corrected inline.

## Why

Under bare-bead dispatch the handoff contract lives only in the agent's prompt;
a pool recycle between push and reassign strands the branch (happened twice in
gas-city). The v2-workflow durability point is now documented where dispatchers
choose a formula, so the isolation/handoff/recycle trade-off is explicit.

## Scope

Single file: `internal/bootstrap/packs/core/skills/gc-dispatch/SKILL.md`.
No code, formula, or behavior changes — the described semantics are the current
`gc sling` contract (verified against `gc sling --help` and the formula
`[requires]` blocks at this tree).

Source: gas-city bead gci-dqe (audit parent gci-7x4).

title: docs(dispatch): state the real base_branch resolution order
body:
docs(dispatch): state the real base_branch resolution order (ga-7mh5)

The gc-dispatch skill described a three-tier base_branch order that
omitted the default_branch tiers entirely and ended at "the rig repo's
default branch" — which reads as the origin/HEAD probe. An agent that
cross-checks that sentence with
`git symbolic-ref refs/remotes/origin/HEAD` can conclude the wrong base
and hand-rebase work that was already based correctly.

The resolver itself is not defective: SlingFormulaTargetBranch already
places a rig's recorded default_branch (tiers 2-3) ahead of the
origin/HEAD probe (tier 4). The documentation is what misled readers.

This updates the skill to state all four tiers, names default_branch as
the knob for a repo whose mainline differs from origin/HEAD, shows the
city.toml stanza, and tells the reader to confirm with
`gc rig list --json` instead of inferring from origin/HEAD (tier 4 only).

The accompanying tests close a real gap rather than restating the
resolver tests: buildSlingFormulaVars — the wiring that decides whether
base_branch is injected at all — had no coverage. If that injection stops
firing, the var falls through to the formula's own "main" default and
every polecat branch is cut from the wrong branch silently, because an
absent var is indistinguishable from an authored default at render time.

Source: dc8327db3 (ga-7mh5), adapted for upstream (soften fork/ROE
framing to generic "repo whose mainline differs from origin/HEAD").

title: docs(core-skills): fix five doc defects reported in #4488
body:
Fixes #4488.

Five documentation defects in `internal/bootstrap/packs/core/skills/`, all re-verified against the running binary immediately before this PR (`go version -m $(which gc)`: `vcs.revision=730c9b2e0a99e29dc9aefc1ec58b14d8da1b36ef`, `vcs.modified=false`).

1. **Dangerous, in gc-dispatch/SKILL.md** — `gc convoy check`/`gc convoy autoclose` descriptions were inverted. `check` takes no id and is an unscoped city-wide auto-close mutation; `autoclose` is the scoped one requiring `<bead-id>`. A reader who copies the doc's `gc convoy check <id>` gets an argument error, and the doc's own `autoclose` line (no id) models "fix" as dropping the argument — which yields the unscoped sweep under the name that reads as a safe check. Swapped the descriptions, fixed the arg placeholders, and marked `check` as mutating.
2. **gc-work/SKILL.md** — documented a claim path (`gc hook show <agent>`, `gc agent claim <agent> <id>`) whose subcommands don't exist. Replaced with the real `gc hook --claim` path, and fixed two more dead flags in the same section (`--label`/`--note` → `--add-label`/`--append-notes`), plus a race caveat on `bd update --claim`.
3. **Four more dead flags/commands**: `gc dashboard --port` (no such flag — replaced examples with real ones: `--no-open`, `serve`), `gc order check <name>` (takes no name), and a `gc skills dashboard` reference (top-level command is `skill`, not `skills`, and no `dashboard` subcommand exists under it either — pointed at the gc-dashboard skill by name instead).
4. **gc-dashboard/SKILL.md self-contradiction** — the per-city `[api]` port section didn't note that supervisor mode overrides it, which contradicted the "per-city `[api]` ports are ignored" statement later in the same file. Added the precedence note where the config is first introduced.
5. **gc-mail/SKILL.md** — `archive`/`delete` were presented as routine operations with no indication that both permanently delete the underlying bead (they're the same operation under two names; there's no reversible "put this away" path). Added an explicit warning and pointed at `mark-read` as the non-destructive alternative.

Also documented three formulas that ship in the core pack but were missing from gc-dispatch/SKILL.md's formula catalogue (`mol-prompt-synth`, `mol-review-quorum`, `mol-scoped-work`) — a smaller sixth item from the same issue.

**Verification**: `go test ./internal/bootstrap/packs/core/... ./internal/config/... ./internal/doctor/... ./internal/materialize/... ./internal/validation/...` all pass.

Not in scope for this PR: `gc mail delete --help`'s own description text (in `cmd/gc/cmd_mail.go`) also undersells what the command does — the issue's "sharper half" — but that's a code change, not a skill-doc fix; flagging it here in case a maintainer wants it as a follow-up.

title: Five documentation defects in the core skill pack, one of them dangerous
body:
We run a multi-agent Gas City where agents read the core skills as their operating manual, so
these surfaced as behaviour rather than as reading. Reporting them as one batch since they share a
cause. Everything below was re-measured against the running binary immediately before filing; where
a claim did not survive that re-measurement we dropped it rather than send it (notes at the end).

PROVENANCE, cited by revision rather than version string because ours is a source build:
    go version -m $(which gc)
      mod          github.com/gastownhall/gascity v1.1.1-0.20260720161128-730c9b2e0a99
      vcs.revision 730c9b2e0a99e29dc9aefc1ec58b14d8da1b36ef
      vcs.modified false
Skill files are from the same tree, at internal/bootstrap/packs/core/skills/.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1. DANGEROUS — a destructive command is documented as a read-only check, and the pair is inverted

gc-dispatch/SKILL.md, lines :166 and :168 (line :167 between them is `gc convoy stranded`,
omitted here only for brevity):
    :166  gc convoy check <id>        # Check if all beads done
    :168  gc convoy autoclose         # Close convoys where all beads done

Both lines are backwards. Measured:
    gc convoy check --help
      "Scan open convoys and auto-close any where all child issues are resolved. ... the convoy is
       automatically closed and an event is recorded."
      Usage: gc convoy check [flags]          <- takes NO id; it is a CITY-WIDE MUTATION
    gc convoy autoclose --help
      "Auto-close completed convoys for a closed bead"
      Usage: gc convoy autoclose <bead-id>    <- REQUIRES the id; this is the scoped one

So the command documented as a per-convoy read-only "check" is an unscoped sweep that closes every
eligible convoy in the city, and the command documented as the sweep is the scoped one.

THE REALISTIC PATH TO HARM is not copying the doc verbatim — `gc convoy check <id>` errors on the
unexpected argument, which is a doc defect accidentally preventing a behavioural one. It is a reader
who hits that error and "fixes" it by DROPPING the argument, which the adjacent autoclose line
explicitly models. That yields the city-wide sweep, described in the same table as a check.

Suggested minimum: swap the two descriptions, remove `<id>` from the check line, add `<bead-id>` to
autoclose, and mark check as mutating.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
2. gc-work documents a claim path whose subcommands do not exist

gc-work/SKILL.md:64-65:
    gc hook show <agent>                   # Show what's on an agent's hook
    gc agent claim <agent> <id>            # Put a bead on an agent's hook

Neither `gc hook show` nor `gc agent claim` is a real subcommand.

ON THE TEST USED, because two obvious tests give two different wrong answers and we got burned by
both before settling: `gc <parent> <sub> --help` EXITS 0 for a nonexistent subcommand and prints the
PARENT's help, so exit status proves nothing (`gc hook show --help` prints `gc hook`'s help, with
`show` swallowed as the positional agent argument). Grepping the parent's "Available Commands" has
the opposite failure — it misses HIDDEN commands, and reported the real `gc convoy autoclose` as
absent. The test that discriminates both ways is whether `<parent> <sub> --help` emits a Usage line
NAMING `<parent> <sub>`:
    gc hook show      -> no        gc convoy check     -> yes
    gc agent claim    -> no        gc convoy autoclose -> yes (hidden, still detected)
    controls: fresh nonsense tokens under each parent -> no
This discriminator was independently hardened before we sent this: hidden commands were enumerated
from source (91 `Hidden: true` sites at this revision) and the test run against seven real hidden
parent+sub pairs — all detected — plus five fresh negative controls, all rejected. Zero false
absents. LIMIT WORTH STATING: it is validated for TWO-LEVEL parent+sub only; three-level probes
returned 0 for real and fake alike, so it is not validated there. No claim in this report is
three-level.

Same section also recommends `bd update --claim`. That flag DOES exist, so this is a
recommendation rather than a defect — but in a multi-agent city it races, and we forbid it in our own
conventions in favour of the atomic `gc hook --claim`. Worth a caveat in the skill if upstream agrees.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
3. Flags and commands that no longer exist

Each verified against the running binaries:
    bd --dir                  no such flag; the real one is -C/--directory ("Change to this
                              directory before running the command (like git -C)")
    bd update --label         no such flag (--add-label)
    bd update --note          no such flag (--append-notes)
    gc dashboard --port       no such flag
    gc order check <name>     takes no name; Usage: gc order check [flags]
    gc skills ...             top-level command is `skill`, not `skills`
                              (referenced at gc-city/SKILL.md:64, "See `gc skills dashboard`")

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
4. gc-dashboard contradicts itself about per-city [api] ports

Not a flat error — the file disagrees with itself, which is why we report it as an inconsistency
rather than a correction:
    :23-24  presents an [api] / port = 9443 configuration premise
    :39     states that in this mode, per-city [api] ports are IGNORED
    :47     `gc dashboard --port 3000   # Same, custom dashboard port` (and see 3: no such flag)
A reader following :23-24 configures something :39 says has no effect.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
5. gc-mail presents two destructive operations as routine — AND `gc mail delete --help` misdescribes
   what the command does, in the reassuring direction

gc-mail/SKILL.md:33,36 list them among ordinary operations with nothing indicating they destroy
content irrecoverably:
    gc mail archive <id>                   # Archive a message
    gc mail delete <id>                    # Delete a message
"Archive" in particular reads as reversible filing to anyone who has used email.

THE SHARPER HALF IS IN THE COMMAND'S OWN HELP, not the skill:
    gc mail delete --help
      "Delete one or more messages BY CLOSING THE BEADS. Same effect as archive but with different
       user intent."
That description is not accurate. In internal/mail/beadmail/beadmail.go:
    :507-508   // Delete is an alias for Archive.
               func (p *Provider) Delete(id string) error { ... }
    :345-372   func (p *Provider) Archive(id string) error — BOTH branches call p.store.Delete(id)
               (the already-closed path at :357 and the normal path at :365)
    :825       your own comment: "Provider.Archive/Provider.Delete mean eager delete"
So the operation the help calls "closing the beads" DELETES the bead. The distinction matters
because a CLOSED bead stays readable and a DELETED one does not — and the reader most likely to be
misled is the careful one, who checks --help before running something destructive.
Suggested minimum: correct the delete help text to say it removes the bead, and add a warning line
to both skill entries. If a non-destructive "put this away" path exists, pointing at it from both
would be worth more than either fix alone.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
6. Three core formulas ship undocumented in the core skill that catalogues formulas

gc-dispatch/SKILL.md catalogues 12 formulas. These three ship in the same core pack and are absent
from it:
    internal/bootstrap/packs/core/formulas/mol-prompt-synth.toml
    internal/bootstrap/packs/core/formulas/mol-review-quorum.toml
    internal/bootstrap/packs/core/formulas/mol-scoped-work.toml

WHAT WE ARE NOT CLAIMING, because we checked and it did not hold: our first draft said "8 of the 12
documented formulas are not installed, including the one the skill calls the Production default".
That is true of OUR city and is not your defect — all 8 exist in the pack; we simply have not
installed them. We dropped that claim rather than send it. Only the three above are a documentation
gap.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
WHY THESE SURFACED TOGETHER

Our agents' skill directory symlinked into a pack checkout several weeks older than the one
`gc skill list` reported, so two different copies were live at once and agents read the older. We
have re-materialised our sink and that half is ours, not yours. But re-reading the CURRENT checkout
is how we found that all six items above are still present in it — these are not stale-cache
artifacts.

title: docs: clarify gc session kill continuity; point context-inject advice at gc handoff
body:
## The juicy parts

The current `gc session kill` help calls it a way to unstick a session "without losing its conversation history." Gas City does not promise that — bead continuity survives (hooks, assignments, lifecycle all still point at the same bead), but provider conversation resume is attempted at best, not guaranteed. A user who reads the help as a guarantee reaches for `kill` in cases where they should not.

The second half is not purely cosmetic: the advisory and urgent context-usage tiers are injected into running agents, and today they tell an agent at high context to run `gc session reset`. `gc handoff` is the better default there — it writes the continuation note first, and it degrades sensibly for attended sessions the controller cannot restart. So this changes what agents are told to do near the recycle threshold, which is worth a look even though the diff is text.

## Summary

Two tiny, adjacent doc/UX touch-ups:

1. `gc session kill` help: clarify what continuity is actually guaranteed — bead/work continuity always survives; provider *conversation* resume is not guaranteed. The current "without losing its conversation history" wording over-promises.
2. `context_inject` advisory/urgent tiers: recommend `gc handoff` instead of `gc session reset`. Handoff is attended-safe and self-mails a continuation note, which is the better default when a session is running low on context.

## Motivation

The kill-continuity wording predates the current lifecycle behavior and reads as a stronger promise than the system makes; #3858 recently poked the controller on `gc session kill` to revive named sessions promptly, but didn't touch the help text. And since both `gc handoff` (`cmd_handoff.go`) and `gc session reset` exist, the context-inject nudge currently points agents at `reset` when `handoff` is the safer, continuity-preserving path for the advisory/urgent case.

Both are low-risk and align with the existing command model rather than adding anything.

## What changed

- `cmd/gc/cmd_session.go` + `docs/reference/cli.md`: kill-continuity wording.
- `cmd/gc/context_inject.go`: advisory/urgent tiers reference `gc handoff`.
- Test updates for both.

## Testing

- `go build ./...`; `go test ./cmd/gc/ -run 'Kill|ContextInject'` passes locally.

## Open questions / happy to adjust

- Split into two PRs (docs vs the context-inject copy) if you'd rather keep them separate?
- If the `handoff`-over-`reset` guidance conflicts with any intended positioning of `gc session reset`, we'll defer to your framing.

## References

#3858.

title: docs(tutorials): use relative .md links for GitHub + Mintlify
body:
## Summary

Cross-tutorial links in `docs/tutorials/` used absolute extensionless Mintlify URLs like `/tutorials/02-agents`. Those work on the deployed docs site but 404 in GitHub's markdown renderer and in IDE previews, where the `.md` files are viewed directly.

This PR switches them to relative `.md` links (`02-agents.md`) so the same links work in both contexts.

## Why it works in both viewers

**GitHub renderer.** Relative `.md` paths resolve against the current file's directory. `02-agents.md` from `docs/tutorials/01-cities-and-rigs.md` resolves to `docs/tutorials/02-agents.md`, which is the file we want.

**Mintlify.** Mintlify's own docs say "Relative paths and paths with extensions do not work in production" by default — but `docs/docs.json` already declares explicit redirects for every tutorial:

```json
{ "source": "/tutorials/01-cities-and-rigs.md", "destination": "/tutorials/01-cities-and-rigs" }
```

(one per tutorial 01–07). Mintlify renders the link `02-agents.md` verbatim as `href="02-agents.md"`. The browser resolves it against the current page `/tutorials/01-cities-and-rigs` → `/tutorials/01-cities-and-rigs.md`, hits the 307 redirect → lands on `/tutorials/02-agents` with a 200.

## Verification

Ran `./mint.sh dev` locally and walked every `.md` link end-to-end with `curl -L`:

- All 20 body cross-tutorial links followed the redirect chain to 200 on the canonical extensionless URL.
- All 7 index-table links followed the redirect chain to 200.

## Caveats

- Production link integrity depends on Mintlify hosting honoring the `redirects` block in `docs.json` (which it does — `mint dev` is parity).
- Removing any of those redirects later silently breaks every `.md` link in the tutorials. `test/docsync/TestLocalMarkdownLinks` is permissive about extension form in Mintlify trees, so it would not catch that regression.

## Test plan

- [ ] `make check-docs` passes
- [ ] Spot-check on the deployed docs site that a cross-tutorial link (e.g. Tutorial 01 → 02) still navigates correctly
- [ ] Open `docs/tutorials/01-cities-and-rigs.md` on GitHub and confirm the link to Tutorial 02 lands on `docs/tutorials/02-agents.md`
